faq.q: Why do I feel so embarrassed?
faq.a: Embarrassment comes when you think others have seen you make a mistake or look silly. Your brain cares about what people think, because getting along with others matters to humans.
When you feel embarrassed, your body releases adrenaline and the tiny blood vessels in your cheeks widen. More warm blood flows near the skin, so your face looks red and feels hot.
asks: What makes your cheeks go red?

faq.a: Yes, everyone does, from children to presidents. Embarrassment is a normal human feeling, and a blush can even make people like and trust you more.

faq.q: How do I stop feeling embarrassed?
faq.a: Take a slow breath, smile, and if you can, laugh it off. Remind yourself that everyone makes mistakes and that the feeling will pass quickly.
asks: What do I do when I am embarrassed?

faq.q: Do people really notice my mistakes?
faq.a: Much less than you think! Scientists call it the spotlight effect: we feel as if a spotlight is on us, but most people are busy thinking about themselves.

facts: In a 2000 study, students wearing an embarrassing T-shirt guessed about half the room noticed it, but only about a quarter really did: this is called the spotlight effect.
Charles Darwin wrote about blushing in his 1872 book on emotions, calling it the most human of all expressions.
